source.rounding: Census counts and totals are randomly rounded independently to multiples of 5 or 10. The sum of categories can differ from the published total; percentages calculated from rounded counts need not sum to 100%.

definitions.populationGroup: Population-group responses to Question 25; this variable differs from both ethnic or cultural origin and the derived visible minority variable.
definitions.singleResponse: IDs 3–14 are single-response categories. Multiple answers are retained in ID 15 instead of counted again in individual groups.
definitions.indigenousPeoples: ID 87 reflects Yes to Question 24. It is not the Indigenous identity variable.

footnotes.englishText: "Population group" refers to whether the person reports being White, South Asian, Chinese, Black, Filipino, Arab, Latin American, Southeast Asian, West Asian, Korean, Japanese or another population group. These specific groups are the mark-in categories used in the population group question (Question 25), which collects data to derive the visible minority population for employment equity purposes.

The population group variable provides a distribution of single and selected combinations of multiple responses to the population group question. For estimates of the visible minority population, please use the variable "Visible minority."

For more information on visible minority and population group variables, including information on their classifications, the questions from which they are derived, data quality and their comparability with other sources of data, please refer to the Visible Minority and Population Group Reference Guide, Census of Population, 2021.

The abbreviation "n.i.e." means "not included elsewhere." This category includes persons who provided a response that is not associated with any of the other population groups. Examples of such responses include, for example, "Algerian," "Armenian," "Brazilian," "Coptic," "Cuban," "Guyanese," "Israeli," "Jamaican," "Jewish," "Kurdish," "Mongolian," "Pacific Islander," "Polynesian," "South African," "Tibetan" and "West Indian."

This category includes respondents who reported “Yes” to Question 24 (“Is this person First Nations, Métis or Inuk (Inuit)?”). These respondents were not asked the population group question (Question 25). However, their information is included in the population group variable so that it reflects the entire Canadian population.

Please note that this category provides a different estimate of the Indigenous population than the variable “Indigenous identity,” which is used in many 2021 Census tables. Indigenous identity includes those who identify as First Nations (North American Indian), Métis and/or Inuk (Inuit), and/or those who report being Registered or Treaty Indians (that is, registered under the Indian Act of Canada), and/or those who have membership in a First Nation or Indian band.

For more information on variables specific to Indigenous peoples, including information on their classifications, the questions from which they are derived, data quality and their comparability with other sources of data, please refer to the Indigenous Peoples Reference Guide, Census of Population, 2021.

Population group  Population group refers to whether the person reports being White, South Asian, Chinese, Black, Filipino, Arab, Latin American, Southeast Asian, West Asian, Korean, Japanese and/or another population group. These specific groups are the mark-in categories used in a question which collects data on the visible minority population for employment equity purposes.
